messages.text: Mom's 10:15 got moved to 11:40, and the pharmacy said the paperwork still needs one signature.
Mom's 10:30 slot is still on. I can get her there if you can handle County Market after work.
I wrote a new order on the kitchen pad. I'll handle the signature, then sit in the car a few minutes before groceries.
That works. I'll bring the receipt book too; she asked where Dad's old insurance folder went.
I'll take the grocery part. Don't stack every errand on yourself before noon.
Top drawer by the phone last time. I'll swing by Ridgeview after and check the vase while I'm out.
Thank you. I'm going to stretch first and leave the house at 10:50 instead of rushing.
Thanks. I'll pick up the groceries and stop in before supper.
Mom found Grandma Kramer's old noodle card in the blue tin. Do you want it for the church supper table?
Yes, tuck it in your purse. I can copy it before Sunday if the basement copier is working.
Also found the Richland County reunion photo with all those pale Kramers squinting by the barn.
That sounds like our side all right. Bring it and I will ask Pastor Jim if we can set both by the coffee urn.
Did you ever finish that WTHI segment you paused during supper?
Yes. The father talking about telling his boys exactly how to sit during a traffic stop stayed with me.
The apartment part too. Same pay stubs, different callbacks.
That is what I keep thinking about. It is not just one bad day when the same doors keep opening slower for some families.
Can you put the pantry note where folks will see it? We are short cereal and canned fruit again.
I shared it from the food bank page and added the Saturday hours. I turned off the extra buzzing after one fellow started picking at the wording.
Good. The note is enough. We need cans, not a long thread.
Exactly. I will check it after lunch and leave the rest alone.
Did you ever circle a week for that Cape house idea, or are you still watching the numbers?
Still watching. The March transfer went in, but I am leaving the top line where it is.
Makes sense. Lavender pictures can sit on the refrigerator a little longer.
They are right by the grocery list. Cape first if we can keep everyone under one roof.
I put your Newton library slip on the table. Two holds came in, one with Frances Perkins on the cover and one about that bridge lady.
Thank you. I’ll pick them up after work tomorrow and set the Baez record by the chair tonight.
Keep the volume low if you do. I’m turning in early after overtime.
Mom's pickup is at 10:30. Are you stopping at Walgreens first or after?
Before. My refill text came in last night, and I want to ask the counter about that county notice before I haul Mom across town.
Good. I saw the shared screenshot going around and wasn't sure what to make of it.
Same. I'll go by what the counter says and what the county page posted, then we can decide about Mom's appointment.
I found the blue tin from the old house. Buttons, bias tape, and one of Grandma's paper grocery envelopes tucked in it.
Keep it for me. I can still see her making us smooth the wrinkles out before she cut a pattern.
There is also Dad's small-engine receipt book and Mom's penciled adding columns from the front desk.
That sounds like the whole kitchen table from Newton, with you doing homework at the end.
If I come Saturday, is my blue quilt still in the closet or did Caleb take it last time?
Still here. I washed yours and put the ballgame blanket back in Caleb's room after Christmas.
Good. I can bring the clinic cookies if he is coming from Terre Haute too.
He said after his Friday job wraps. I will set the extra plates out.
For Sunday, is Emily coming after that front-desk half day or earlier?
After, I think. Caleb said he may be late too if the panel job over by the Wabash runs long.
Then I will keep the rolls wrapped. Those two are always coming from opposite directions.
Paper says the county board is taking comments Monday about the sheriff office budget.
I may go after Mom's prescription run. I want to hear what the camera costs actually are before folks start hollering.
Ask plain. Last time the deputy at the wreck was decent to us.
He was. That still doesn't mean a county job should run on trust alone.
Saw another big sign for Brant by the Casey's. Same line as the mailer.
The sign doesn't tell me if he can keep a budget straight. I want to hear how he'd handle the road fund and who checks the numbers.
Forum is next Thursday at the high school. We can go after supper if your shoulder's okay.
Let's go. I wrote down three questions, and none of them fit on a bumper sticker.
Did your check hit yet? I want to pay electric before the weekend if it did.
I set the clerk envelope by your chair. The school board page is still folded where you had it.
Yes, the main one shows $3,900 gross on the stub. I put it with your overtime note.
Good. I want to compare the two with the bus route answers before supper.
Good. Keep the little concrete money separate until we see where groceries land.
The sheriff one is on top too. I marked the one who sounded steady on the jail budget.
That is the one I leaned toward, but I want to read the courthouse questionnaire again.
I will. That one is only $250, so it can cover fuel and Mom's prescriptions.
Farm & Home has those safety-toe ones on the end cap again. Same pair you liked last year, I think.
I saw the flyer. I wrote down the size, but I'm only price-checking today.
If the left heel is still rubbing, grab moleskin from the drawer till you decide.
Good thought. The March stack on the counter gets first say.
Are you still coming Sunday or did Ray add Saturday after the rain day?
Sunday still works. I got 8 today with the tear-out and stacking boards, so he is counting that toward the week.
Good. Bring your shoulder wrap if we do groceries. I can cover Mom's prescription run on my lunch Monday.
Thanks. I already set aside gas money and the boot payment, so groceries need to stay close to the list.
I found two red fat quarters in the pantry closet bag. Want me to bring them Thursday?
Yes, please. I'll trade you the little basket pattern and the cream scraps I promised.
Deal. Also, don't stay bent over that table too late tonight if your shoulder is talking.
I'll keep it to one block and tea, then quit.
Do you want the blue folder from the truck before you head out? It has those old 30-hour papers and machine cards.
Yes, please set it by my lunch box. They asked for copies before I sit in with the morning crew lead.
I put the ice pack in there too. Don’t climb back on that backhoe if your shoulder starts barking.
I’m mostly watching the setup today and taking notes on how Rick handles the paperwork.
Do you want me to grab Mom's prescription when I go by Effingham, or did that clinic receipt already hit your stack?
It hit Friday, so I wrote it beside the insurance draft and groceries. Trying to keep the next page nearer 3400 than that ugly March number.
I can take her paper towels and milk this time. You already had fuel and that porch board on there.
Thanks. Mark said one list at a time, so I'm not adding anything extra before church.
Mom's file cabinet still has those Richland Memorial cards. Want me to bring yours when I come by?
Yes please. Mine should be the one with 6/14/71 on the corner. I need it with the courthouse packet.
Found it. Same drawer as the Newton papers and Grandma's old utility receipts.
That drawer is half our life story. Bring the folder and I will make copies tomorrow.
Mom asked why you were hunting through old boxes after church.
Emily wanted a story for that family thing. I found the garage papers from out past Newton, mixed in with sitter notes.
The ones from when you quit chasing every little Saturday job?
Yes. Same packet has my scribble where the opening was off before anyone touched the saw.
Mom asked if Sunday supper is at your place or mine after church.
Mine. I have a chicken in the oven and can put green beans with it if that row is ready.
Good. Need me to bring rolls?
Rolls would help. I still need to jot down which bed got soaked before the rain starts.
Rain may hold off till noon. Are you still going to that tear-out job?
Going, but I told Ray I am not taking the overhead pieces today. I will handle ground cleanup and keep the ladder short.
Good. Do your driveway lap before you leave and take the small brace from the truck.
Already did one slow lap. I will do the hips and circles when I get there before we start.
I put the sacks by the back door. Do you want the folding table in the truck too?
Yes, and the blue tote with hymnals can stay home. We only need the table and the extra coffee urn.
Got it. I will pull around after you finish with the bulletin basket.
Thank you. If we keep the line moving, folks can be through before the rain starts.
Shoulder any better after the yard bags?
Some. I did the doorway stretches and walked the long way to church. Packed egg salad and those little tomatoes so I would not grab drive-through.
Good. Take it easy before bowling. One list at a time.
I only took one from the bathroom bottle this morning. I'll give it time before I even think about another.
I put the mower gas receipt by the coffee maker. Do we need anything besides bread and eggs before I come in?
Just milk. I already pulled two pork chops down for us.
Good. I should be home before the 6:15 tip if traffic stays clear.
I saved your chair and left the remote on the end table.
Overtime ran long. I can edge by the mailbox after supper if you already got the hose out.
I watered the tomatoes and the west bed. Left the hose coiled so it will not kink when you trim.
Smelled like somebody cut hay west of town when I came through. Porch might be better than TV tonight.
That is my vote. We can look at the Cape Cod envelope after the ballgame score, but I want my own porch first.
I picked up the 2x4s. Do you want me to leave the warped one in the truck?
Yes. The short pantry shelf will show every bow once it is loaded. I would rather wait than hang it crooked.
Fair. Linda said they can use that shelf before Saturday if we get it set.
Tell her I said Saturday morning still stands. I will mark the studs after dinner and bring the level.
If I swing through Saturday, can I borrow the outlet tester and the short ladder?
Yes. I put them by the garage freezer and wrote the porch outlet steps on the bench pad: breaker first, gloves, then photo the panel label.
Good. I'll bring the tester back with tomatoes if you've started seeds yet.
Seed trays are on the kitchen square for Sunday after church. My phone will buzz at 6:00 tonight so I don't forget the outside faucet before the cold comes in.
Mom's form is printed. Are you still trying to fit that shoulder place before work Wednesday?
I called them. Earliest cheap slot is 7:20, but the first visit is more than I wanted this week.
Could Mark cover Mom's pharmacy run if you take the early one?
Maybe. I am checking the medical line after I move $35 to the certification one.
Do you still want me to bring the office shred bin Sunday? I found a stack of old papers in my closet.
Yes, bring it. I am sorting the 2006 closing folder and the newer bank letters at the kitchen table.
That kitchen table has seen every folder in the county.
It has, and I am stopping once the house draft and truck slip are clipped for March. No extra store run till then.
Can you still take the cereal table tonight? I’ll get there after I put the lane envelopes in my purse.
Yes. I’ll be there by 5:45 and I can tape the box bottoms before the rush.
Good. If Marcy texts about blue scraps, tell her I found a small bundle by my machine.
I’ll tell her. See you in a bit, and save me that corner spot by the apples.
Dad said the truck parts were more than he thought. Still doing that little Indiana night?
I slid it out of March. One night is not worth crowding the house column and the away column both.
Fair. If the Cape binder needs outlet measurements for a rental, send them when you find one.
I will. For now I am just saving listings that fit the number already on the page.
I brought Dad's tester back. One cord has a nick in it, so don't let him use that one till I tape it right.
A guy on the crew sent me a big thread saying that new shot is a bad idea. You heard anything?
I put a note on it and set it on the washer, away from the good cords.
I haven't seen anything from Dr. Patel's office or the county yet. I can ask Emily what their front desk is handing out.
Figured you'd check the real paper trail before I repeated it.
Good. Also my Terre Haute shift may slide Saturday if the inspector runs late.
Yes. Also remind me Sunday to pack the little white bottle with my purse before we leave after lunch.
Text me when you know. I'll keep supper flexible and start the quilt blocks instead of adding another errand.
Mom, did you still need my laptop Sunday for that online builder class?
If you can bring it, yes. Mine freezes on the scheduling quizzes and the change-order section.
I can. Want me to print those skid-steer and backhoe wallet cards while I’m at the shop?
That would help. I’m keeping everything together before I ask about shadowing Jason on walk-throughs.
You going to that town thing again? Dad said you had questions written on a grocery envelope.
Just three. How often they get refreshers, who reviews the little cameras, and where a person starts if something goes sideways.
Sounds like jobsite rules. We don't wait till somebody gets hurt to explain the steps.
Exactly. Most days folks do the job fine, but the steps still ought to be written down.
Can you take Mom to the pharmacy Tuesday or is your crew already poured into that morning?
I can swap if it rains. The shop still counts only a half day if I use one of those few paid hours.
Save those then. I can drive her if you need to keep the hours.
Thanks. After nearly nine Marches there, I know not to burn them unless I have to.
The bakery shop in Effingham still has that cookie box with the little spool and square-template cutters.
If it is under $18, grab one for me. I won't open it until I finish the blue top.
It is $15.99. The icing cards look fussy but cute.
That can be my Friday-night treat after I put the last border on.
I can get us the end lane tonight if you want more room before first roll.
That would help. I need the extra minutes for hamstrings and hips, and I am keeping the ball swing lower.
I will grab your shoes when I get mine. You just take your lap and come in slow.
Thanks. Still planning to be there. Just doing it smarter tonight.
Bowling at 6:30 if your arm is not too mad after today.
I should make it. We spent the afternoon moving sheets off the trailer and I had the loader for the last hour.
Then I will save you the lighter pantry boxes Saturday. Did the check come through before the power bill?
It did. Forty-two hours on this one, so March is behaving for now.
You skipping bowling tonight or just running late?
Late. Denise took the early round with Mom, then I stayed to sort her mail and set up Friday's pills.
Come when you can. I saved your lane.
Thanks. I also had to find the little flag holder for Dad's spot before the rain starts.
After bowling, remind me which judge names you said to look up. I lost my little note.
Sure. I only wrote down who answered the farm bureau and newspaper questions plainly.
You and Mark go deeper on those county pages than anyone I know.
The courthouse offices affect us more than the noisy ads, so I try not to guess.
Did you ever finish the one you brought to bowling with all the pencil tabs sticking out?
Almost. The chapter on the bridge cables had me stopping every page. I had Baez on low and forgot the laundry.
Bring it Thursday if your shoulder lets you bowl. I want to see what had you frowning so hard.
I’ll put it in my bag with the score sheet.
Mom, did you keep my old glove in the cedar chest or did Emily's stuff get stacked on it?
Your glove is with the baseball photos. Emily's school folders are in the next tote.
I'll grab it when I swing by. Need Dad's tester too if he can spare it.
He put it on the bench. I will leave both totes by the back door.
Are you still going to that noon talk before Mom's prescription pickup?
I am. The man from Olney who spoke Sunday said the rental forms look neutral until you hear what happened at the desk.
Just don't be late getting Mom. She'll be watching the clock.
I won't. I want to hear the rest first, especially the part about job applications getting sorted before anybody meets the person.
Lunch got pushed back. We had three people at the window and the reminder calls stacked up.
Eat when you can. Caleb texted that he found the tester Mark wanted, but he is still across the line until quitting time.
Front desk had three people ask about the clinic ride forms again. They get lost on the website.
Tell him not to bring dusty boots through your kitchen again.
Paper copies would save everyone trouble. Plain form, one phone number, and somebody checking it twice.
Exactly. Same with the evening class vouchers. Good idea, messy handoff.
If it gets people to appointments or into paid work, then make it simple enough to actually use.
I will put him straight through the garage.
The clinic form has a line for extra letters after your name. Leave it empty unless you have one from a program.
Empty is right. I have the Newton diploma copy and my work history page, nothing fancy.
There is also a question about current classes or training hours.
Put no hours there. I am just trying to get this packet done before the June 14 cake plans start.
Did you see Aunt Carol added those birthday pictures? There is one of Dad with cake on his sleeve.
I saved that one and left a heart. I almost answered the cousin who was fussing under it, then thought better and went back to the album.
That is probably best. The cake picture is the only useful part.
I sent it to your brother too. He will laugh at Mark's face.
For the office bulletin, can I use your story about starting on a crew while Caleb and I were small?
Keep it plain. I had two envelopes on the table then: more register hours or Larry's Monday crew.
Was that the garage where you found the bad number?
Out by Newton, yes. I remember checking twice because the stack was waiting.
You went to that forum, didn't you? Pantry folks were all talking about the loud fellow in the red tie.
Loud doesn't stock shelves or fix delivery hours. The woman at the end had the better answer on the back entrance and Saturday drop-offs.
She was quieter, but she knew the loading schedule.
That counts more to me than a room clapping.
If bowling runs late Thursday, are you two still trying to catch the late game?
Mark said he can reheat supper while I change, so yes if my shoulder behaves.
That sounds like your usual setup. I will bring the pantry signup sheet before league starts.
New volunteer is nervous about the inventory sheets. Could you walk her through the canned vegetables side?
I can. Put her with me first hour, and I will show her the count marks before we open the boxes.
Thank you. Also that shelf you and Mark put up is holding straight even with the heavy bags.
Good. I checked it twice because those bags shift. I will bring extra labels too.
I can swing by Rural King after pantry sorting if you still want me to look at the black pants rack.
Just check the tag price, please. Mine are faded but holding.
Want me to see if the boot inserts are still by the register too?
Yes, inserts are the safer errand this round.
I can swing by after I return Dad's socket set. Anything you want moved while I'm there?
If you can lift the big bag by the zucchini spot, that saves my shoulder.
Sure. You still making soup tonight?
Yes, with pantry beans. I need to finish the east side watering first and write down the basil starts.
If you and Dad do the longer trip later, would you still want me to swing by on Sundays for the plants?
Only if we are gone more than a few days. I would rather plan it so we pull back into Newton before the porch pots get thirsty.
That sounds like you. I can bring those clinic pens tomorrow when I come over.
Good. If you get here near dusk, come around back. Mark and I should be finishing the side beds.
Want me to bring the coupon booklet tomorrow? The cereal and coffee ones are actually decent.
Bring it, please. Groceries, truck gas, and the electric bill are what keep bumping the page up.
Do you still have that 3600 note on the fridge?
Yes, and I circled it after the last fuel fill-up. We will eat what is in the freezer this week.
Bowling crowd is meeting at Rusty Rail after league. Want me to save you a seat?
Save one, but I'm bringing my lemon water. My shoulder is talking, and I still need to sort pantry boxes in the morning.
I'll keep you away from the heavy cans. Did you eat or are you doing the vending machine thing?
Lunch bag is in the car: chicken wrap, cucumber, and the last jar of our salsa.
I checked the road by the old place. County gravel is rough but passable if we go slow tomorrow.
Good. I want one more look at the stones before the spring rain settles in.
Pack sunscreen. You and Denise both came home pink last time, and it was barely March.
I will. After that we can drop the casserole at church and head back before dark.
Do you still want the green coat from the rummage sale, or should I put it back in the donation bag?
Bring it Sunday. Grandma would say the lining has another year in it if I take my time.
I found a Jasper County program in the pocket. Names listed for Mom, Dad, you, and Denise.
Save that too. Those little programs always ended up in Mom's drawer with her office pencils.
Water heater quote came in at $2,000 even. I can price parts again tomorrow.
That is bigger than the house line. We would have to pull from the rainy-day account and probably float some on the card.
One list at a time. Do you want me to hold off buying the yard stuff?
Yes, leave travel and medical alone until I know what the dentist says Thursday.
Dad said the truck place sent another receipt. Want me to file it when I come by for the tester?
Please. Put it in the blue folder behind the house statement, same drawer as the tax papers.
Need anything from Terre Haute while I am there?
No, we are holding to the list. Paid Visa in full this morning and I want the savings line left at 400.
At lunch everyone keeps sharing that clip from the courthouse steps. Are you watching it?
No, I read the minutes from last fall instead. I want to know who showed up for the nursing transport vote.
That sounds like you. Did the quiet woman have a record?
She was there, asked two plain questions, and her numbers matched the clerk's report. That matters.
Don’t forget the roster sheet tonight. I think we’re on the pair closest to the soda machine.
It’s in my purse. I’ll come straight from Newton Food Bank after the bread shelf is filled.
I’ll warm up slow then. Your shoulder did better last time after you skipped the heavy balls.
Good plan. I’ll bring the lemon bars Marcy liked if they don’t get crushed.
Pantry truck is coming at 8:00 instead of 9:30 Saturday, and they sent extra canned goods.
I can sort labels for one hour, then I need to pass the heavy boxes to someone else.
I'll put you at the table with the clipboard. Bring that neat list of yours.
That works. I already crossed off bowling practice and will take a short walk after supper.
Ma, the online form kicked back because the service-number box was blank. Did they need something from Dad?
No, it said skip if none. I never had a number for that box.
Got it. Also Emily said you picked 55 candles for June. That right?
Yes, but do not buy the noisy ones. Plain candles and a cake from Newton will do.
I can drop Mark's crimper off Saturday if 70 isn't backed up.
That works. Emily may come after the Effingham errands if her phones don't run late.
I will bring the crimper and grab those jars. Leaving Terre Haute around 8 if the morning call stays short.
Foreman at our site said they need another safety person for mornings. You ever think about that instead of crawling around old houses?
I have. I know the crews and I know what gets skipped when everyone is rushing.
You would be good at it. Less hauling, more telling people to use their head.
That is the idea. I can still put in a day, but I am learning where to spend it.
Mom's ID paperwork is in the blue folder. Do you still have that old ticket receipt from the courthouse drawer?
Only the seatbelt warning from years back and the fender-bender copy. Nothing else for us to track down.
Good. Clerk said simple copies are enough for her appointment.
I'll bring them, then stop by the annex board to see if they posted answers from Monday.
I found a Cape Cod article in Mom's magazine stack. Want me to save it?
Yes, please. Put it with the lavender-field clipping if it is still in the blue folder.
It is. Also, the dentist bill came, so I assume you are leaving that June motel note in pencil.
Pencil for now. I am not borrowing from the amount I wrote down in January.
The Newton community page has the library craft night moved to Tuesday. Can you send it to Mom's neighbor?
Sent. I also checked the church page because the bulletin had a different time.
I saw somebody griping under the library notice.
I did too. I copied the time and backed out before I typed anything.
Our office got the updated handout today. Want me to bring one when I come Saturday?
Please. The one Linda's cousin shared had no date on it, and I don't like guessing from a picture.
I'll bring the copy from the nurse's station. Also, did the refill go through okay?
Yes, $11 copay this time. I put it beside the coffee so I don't miss tomorrow morning.
Do you need the car at noon or can I take the truck for parts?
I need the car from 12:15 to 2. Mom has lab work, and Denise is covering the grocery list after.
I'll take the truck. Want me to pull the wreath box down for Sunday?
Yes, please. Denise and I are changing Dad's flowers after church.
The used shop in Effingham has a Mary Harris Jones one in the front window. Want me to grab it before they close?
Yes, if it’s under $10. I’ve got the Gilbreth pages from the library due Monday, so that one can wait on the nightstand.
Found it for $7. Also saw a Baez cassette by the register, but the case is cracked.
Leave the cracked case. The record at home still plays fine.
The pantry line was long after you left. That new volunteer from Robinson asked if you found the article she mentioned.
I did. It matched what she said about her nephew being watched in the store before he even picked anything up.
Hard to hear that over coffee, but I'm glad she talked with us.
Me too. I would miss a lot if I only heard from people whose errands and callbacks go like mine.
Are you still coming to pantry sorting after that porch repair this morning?
Yes, just a short patch job. I promised myself no more than two hours before lunch.
Good. Your shoulder was talking during bowling.
I know. The extra cash helps, but I still need Monday's regular hours intact.
I grabbed that metal parts tray from Mark's bench. It has Grandpa's initials scratched under the grease.
That's Dad's old tray. He kept bolts for mowers and planters in it.
There was a folded flour sack in there too, patched into a tool wrap. Yours?
Mine after Grandma showed me how. Denise and I used to argue over who got the neat scraps.
If I come through Newton next weekend, do you still need the folding tables moved from the church closet?
Yes, please. The potluck signup is already full, and I put our cabbage rolls on the second line.
Are those from the stained recipe card Denise was talking about?
Same box. Grandma wrote half of it in pencil, so I am guessing on the salt again.
I can swing by Newton Sunday and return Dad's socket set. Should I bring lunch or are you and Mark already set?
We are set. I planned enough for the two of us, but I can stretch it if you stop in.
No need. I may just grab the tools and watch an inning with him before heading back.
He will like that. The recliner side is already claimed when the game starts.
I can bring back Dad's saw today. Did he still need more lumber?
No more boards unless something breaks. The lumber ticket and garden bags already made this page higher than a normal one.
I can spot the tomato cages if that helps.
Hold off. I want April sitting between 3400 and 3600 if the insurance and clinic copay behave.
Do you want me to bring the card table today, or are Emily and Caleb using the kitchen one for sorting boxes?
Bring it, please. They are going through the attic tubs after lunch.
Those tubs go way back. I remember the science fair board and Caleb's tiny cleats.
I found Emily's ribbon folder too. I told them they can take what fits in their cars.
Mom, did you still want me to ask at work about moving Grandma's refill pickup?
Yes please. I have her ride marked Wednesday on the kitchen calendar, but my phone says rain by 3:00.
I'll check when I get back from lunch. Want me to call you if they only have Friday?
Call if Friday. I wrote groceries, papers, and the $18 copay in the notebook so Denise and I don't both buy the same things.
Mom's prescription pickup can wait until 3. Did you finish your courthouse list from last week?
Mostly. Mark and I agreed on treasurer and county board, but I am still checking the school tax answers.
That sounds like you. I just need your short version before I go.
I will send it after lunch. I am staying with the practical ones, not the loud postcard people.
Can I borrow Dad's Sawzall Saturday, or is it in your truck?
In my truck till tomorrow. Ray has us opening the back room and I need it with the pry bars.
No rush. I get paid Friday too, so I can bring pizza and swap you for tomatoes from the freezer.
Deal. If tomorrow runs past 45 for the week, I am sleeping before we talk tools.
Mom’s pharmacy run is done. Are you still tied up after supper?
Yes, I’ve got the lanes tonight. Linda is picking me up at 6:05.
Then I’ll take the paperwork to her house tomorrow. Jo can leave the binding clips with Marcy.
That works. I’ll drop the pantry key back in the lockbox before Linda gets here.
You still bowling tomorrow, or are you saving that shoulder after all those forms?
I’ll bowl light. I spent tonight pricing a small porch frame and a two-man concrete patch, so at least I wasn’t lifting.
That sounds more like your notebook work. Did the Saturday clinic take your check?
Yes, $85. I’m bringing gloves, kneepads, and the folder with all my cards in case they want copies.
If you see a used miter saw near Terre Haute for under 80, send it my way.
I found one in the Newton listings for 65, but the comments are already getting sharp over pickup order.
Mom, did you ever decide on that county board race? Guy at work said just pick the usual column and be done.
Just message the seller direct if it looks decent.
I don't do it that way for town offices. I marked the one who answered plainly about bids, ambulance shifts, and the pantry driveway.
The quieter one from the forum?
Yes. She had receipts, and I couldn't find anyone saying she played games with the books.
Found your old folding rule in the toolbox. Want me to bring it Sunday?
That is what I did. I sent you the link and did not touch the comments.
Bring it. That rule was in my apron when I stopped piecing together shifts and stuck with Larry's jobs.
Same one from the garage story?
Yes, the one where I made them recheck the bay before boards got marked.
Terre Haute job board has a wiring refresher that pays the fee if you finish. Half the guys say the signup is a maze.
That is where they lose people. Put the class dates, bus route, and one real contact on the first page.
You would have that clipboard fixed in ten minutes.
Only because I have watched good help get wasted when nobody minds the details.
Are the kids both coming for your birthday supper?

events.title: Ray crew - Maple St porch forms
events.notes: Pack gloves, tape, chalk line, 25' rule. Check rain radar before leaving; Ray said pour may slide if the lot is soft.

events.title: Stretches, block loop, pack lunch
events.notes: Use tomato slices from freezer bag. Check bottle count before taking anything extra for shoulder.

events.title: Back beds: south half, update notebook
events.notes: Check tomato and pepper starts before work. Mark south half done; leave north half for Thursday. Pull chicken from freezer for pot pie.

events.title: Check First Newton drafts
events.notes: House draft clears Friday; truck draft next Tuesday. Move only grocery cushion after both post.

events.title: Call Newton Dental after payroll posts
events.notes: Ask whether the $400-ish balance can be split before moving the March slot. Check medical tab first, leave home repair line alone.

events.title: Closet check: soles, jeans, jacket
events.notes: Write down sizes before Farm & Home sale flyer expires. Compare with last spring's receipt envelope.

events.title: Binder scan: 30-hr card, loader/backhoe cards, bid notes
events.notes: Put copies in blue folder before Friday. Add concrete/framing numbers from notebook and keep wrist stretches between pages.

events.title: Sort March envelope before bills
events.notes: Tuck main check stub with the insurance line, PTO/sick balance slip, and the porch-frame patch receipt. Leave concrete quote blank until Jim calls.

events.title: Kitchen table: county clerk packet
events.notes: Circle sheriff forum notes, school board names, and tax levy page before recycling the mailer stack.

events.title: Blue star blocks after supper
events.notes: Press strips, square up corners, put Marlene's envelope with the green print pieces by the back door.

events.title: Kitchen table folder
events.notes: Pencil total: 3900. Check mortgage stub, Ameren, Casey's card, grocery slips, insurance draft, clinic receipt, Rural King, and lumber ticket.

events.title: Copy documents for county packet
events.notes: Take blue folder: old Newton diploma, marriage paper, and the card from Richland Memorial. Ask clerk about blank sections before signing.

events.title: Pantry boxes, then Denise quilt pieces
events.notes: Bring canned-goods list, square ruler, blue thread, and the two blocks with corners that need lining up.

events.title: Pick up holds + return CD
events.notes: Holds shelf: Perkins, Roebling. Return scratched Baez disc; ask if the clean copy is back.

events.title: Chili bowls and game on TV
events.notes: Set out two bowls before first pitch; Mark bringing crackers after work.

events.title: Sort cans and paper sacks
events.notes: Bring tape, marker, and the clipboard list. Check dates on soups and cereal before setting up Saturday tables.

events.title: West bed, hose washer, Cape Cod envelope
events.notes: Check the hose washer by the garage spigot. Water the west bed after supper. Count trip cash at kitchen table if Mark is back before dark; porch after if the county road smells fresh-cut again.

events.title: Find old crew notebook
events.notes: Look for folder marked west of Newton garage. Check page with kids' sitter receipt, counter-shift schedule, and the 23 ft / 23 ft 8 in lumber note.

events.title: March house money pass
events.notes: Electric due 3/8, water due 3/12. Copy totals into blue bag notebook. Hold $42 aside if Mark gets the mower belt before Friday.

events.title: Arrive early before league
events.notes: Slow lap outside first; hamstrings, hips, circles. Easy first game, no showing off.

events.title: Lane 7 - Linda has score sheets
events.notes: Bring wrist tape. Ask Linda if the canned beans from St. Mary’s need sorting before Saturday.

events.title: Walk, stretch, kitchen list
events.notes: Before pantry sorting: bills due dates, Mom pickup plan, repair receipt check. Leave one open hour after lunch.

events.title: Walgreens refill + printouts
events.notes: Pick up 90-day refill. Ask counter to compare county notice with CDC sheet before Sunday dinner talk.

events.title: Move March overnight hold to June folder
events.notes: Check motel cancel-by date. Keep Cape notes and Provence clipping in the same binder pocket. Do not raise the 2026 ceiling.

events.title: Mom: pharmacy, bank papers, Ridgeview flowers
events.notes: Denise drives. Bring checkbook, pill organizer, and two red geraniums.

events.title: Service, basement coffee, family table setup
events.notes: Bring blue tin recipe copy, Kramers reunion photo, tape, and two pans of noodles. Check pantry shelf after coffee.

events.title: After-service table talk
events.notes: Stay for Mrs. Watkins' invited guests from the apartment committee; bring cookies. Ask about lease screening, bus stops, and the school pickup issue from last week's bulletin.

events.title: Sunday dinner - Emily and Caleb
events.notes: Make roast, send leftovers with Emily for Effingham, set aside tomatoes and Mark's socket set for Caleb.

events.title: Family dinner - leave soup warm
events.notes: Emily after morning phones; Caleb after breaker swap on the west route. Save tomatoes and small socket set by back door.

events.title: Post church supper notice and check quilt block replies
events.notes: Use St. Mary's post photo; answer time/place only. If the quilt thread drifts into county complaints, close it and come back tomorrow.

events.title: Denise - sort cedar chest items
events.notes: Set aside Grandma's thimble, apron pattern pieces, Mom's receipt pads, Dad's repair manuals, and the school photo sleeve with both of us in it.

events.title: County board public comment
events.notes: Ask about grant options for worn cameras, yearly storage fees, and whether the public concern form can be found without calling three offices.

events.title: County board candidate forum
events.notes: Bring notebook. Ask about ambulance coverage, road fund oversight, food pantry delivery access, and who signs off on monthly bills.

events.title: Boxes and intake list
events.notes: Take marker, gloves, and the folded fabric bag for Jo after cleanup.

events.title: Before leaving: van folder + Cape Cod jar
events.notes: Put insurance card in glove box. Add $25 to trip envelope. Check tire gauge and write mileage in small notebook.

events.title: Firehouse stop before work
events.notes: Bring ID, folded clerk sheet, and Mark's sticky note on county board District 2.

events.title: Oak Lane remodel - plans + wall layout
events.notes: Ray wants west wall marks checked against sheet A-2 before lunch. Bring square, nail pouch, extra pencil, and knee pads.

events.title: Evening class: contracts, quantities, crew sheets
events.notes: Bring calculator, tape notes from slab pour, and folder with backhoe/skid-steer copies. Ask about April hands-on clinic form.

events.title: Call Linda: March box count
events.notes: Ask about cereal shortage, extra tuna, and whether the voucher flyers need a separate stack. Keep final count on one sheet for Saturday.

events.title: Finish border, pack swap bag
events.notes: Chocolate cookie kit after dishes if the miters behave. Add Linda's cream scraps and Ruth's pinwheel sheet to tote.

events.title: Envelope update after payday
events.notes: Set aside truck fuel, groceries, Mom errands. Move boots/black pants card behind April tab unless extra remains.

events.title: Newton Dental estimate call
events.notes: Ask about moving the second visit to April 10 after work. If total stays near $400, use medical line before touching the card.

events.title: Call Emily - old work story
events.notes: Mention kitchen-table choice: store schedule vs Larry's crew. Include garage west of Newton, header number checked before lumber was cut.

events.title: West rows, border strip, casserole prep
events.notes: Water west rows only. Note pepper tray count. Thin border marigolds if soil is soft. Assemble chicken casserole before bowling tomorrow.

events.title: Walk before Caleb visit
events.notes: Bring leftover soup and tomato bread. Shoulder: wait until after supper before deciding on another tablet. Keep porch table cleared for coffee cups.

events.title: Food bank intake + show Tara shelf labels
events.notes: Bring label maker, spare tape, level, and quilt bag for Denise after lunch.

events.title: Drive north of Newton, seed potatoes, back by dusk
events.notes: Pick up seed potatoes and two tomato cages. Take the county road if it is dry. Be back in time to water the porch pots before the ballgame.

events.title: Online info session
events.notes: Foreman / safety coordinator certificate options. Bring notebook. Walk block first so sitting through it goes better.

events.title: March bill folder with Mark
events.notes: Confirm Visa zero after autopay; leave Cape Cod jar alone until house and truck drafts show posted.

events.title: Call Dr. Patel's office
events.notes: Ask about timing from county update; keep Walgreens refill slip in purse for current list. Do not answer Linda's cousin's shared thread until checked.

events.title: Read Herald clipping + call-in notes
events.notes: Compare Sunday's handout with the Herald piece on the body-cam hearing. Write down questions for Linda before pantry sorting: traffic stops, landlord callbacks, and why neighbors describe the same errands so differently.

events.title: Review blue folder before April transfer
events.notes: Print two Cape rentals that sleep everyone. Leave Provence lavender page for later. March overnight stays crossed out until parts and dentist checks clear.

events.title: Church potluck and family clipping table
events.notes: Bring cabbage rolls, Grandma Kramer's clippings, Richland County photo, sunscreen for cemetery stop after lunch.

events.title: Cards game, laundry, leftovers
events.notes: Fold towels during middle innings; make two leftover plates after church.

events.title: Mom paperwork with Denise
events.notes: Review March receipts, refill card, utility bill. Take Dad's framed photo back from the hallway table if Mom is ready.

events.title: Quiet hour before supper
events.notes: Finish Perkins notes; start Jones if time. Side A of Baez LP.
